REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JANUARY 25, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
COUNCILMEMBER JOHNSON WILL PARTICIPATE VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM THE LOBBY AT THE HOTEL ROYAL CONTINENTAL, VIA PARTENOPE 38/44, NAPLES, ITALY 80121, AND THIS AGENDA WILL BE POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, JANUARY 25,
2024, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA. COUNCILMEMBER JOHNSON PARTICIPATED VIA
TELECONFERENCE FROM THE LOBBY AT THE HOTEL ROYAL CONTINENTAL, VIA PARTENOPE
38/44, NAPLES, ITALY 80121, AND THIS AGENDA WAS POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN
ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk Division Manager.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Lady Tigers – Cerritos Youth Basketball Team (Girls Pee
  Wee Division).

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson (via teleconference)
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

 5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Cerritos High School Varsity Football (CIF-Southern Section Champions).

  Big 5 Electronics Inc. (Business Spotlight).

  Cerritos Macerich, LLC (Festival of Friendship – 25th Anniversary).

 6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk Division Manager, provided the following disclaimer concerning
  written comments submitted for all agenda items: Written comments submitted by the
  deadline listed on the agenda are considered public record. Prior to the meeting, the
  Council/Agency members received full-text, unredacted copies of any written comments
  submitted for items listed on the agenda, including general public comments. Public
  requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made during
  regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Case Van der Linden expressed concern regarding a potential Metro light rail transit line
  running through Cerritos and communication from the City to the public, related to this
  issue.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, January 25, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Sam Desai spoke in opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East and submitted a
  document for the official record. He also expressed concern regarding a potential Metro
  light rail transit line running through Cerritos and communication from the City to the
  public, related to this issue. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting
  are considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written
  correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer).

  Ernie Nishii invited the City Council to various upcoming ABC Unified School District events.

  Kirit Chauhan spoke regarding upcoming ABC Unified School District Town Hall meetings
  and expressed concern regarding declining enrollment. He also requested additional
  pickleball courts to be located at Cerritos Park East.

  Margaret Villa requested the City Council take action to support H.Res. 786 – Calling for an
  immediate de-escalation and cease-fire in Israel and occupied Palestine.

  Murali Vasudevan requested additional free-use pickleball courts at Cerritos Park East or
  Heritage Park, inquired about follow-up to City Council consensus items, and inquired
  regarding various City Fiscal Year 2024-2025 annual budget plans.

  Rodolfo Cortes requested the City Council take action to support H.Res. 786 – Calling for an
  immediate de-escalation and cease-fire in Israel and occupied Palestine.

  Al Barlevy expressed concern regarding the City taking action to support H.Res. 786 –
  Calling for an immediate de-escalation and cease-fire in Israel and occupied Palestine.

  Jay Gray requested additional free-use pickleball courts at Cerritos Park East and spoke in
  opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East.

  Written Correspondence:

  David Amin requested additional free-use pickleball courts at City facilities located on the
  east side of Cerritos.

  Bernard Chu requested additional free-use pickleball courts at City facilities located on the
  east side of Cerritos and expressed opposition to the renaming of Cerritos Park East.

  Murali Vasudevan requested additional free-use pickleball courts at City facilities located on
  the east side of Cerritos.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Thursday, January 11, 2024, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Thursday, January
  11, 2024, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, January 25, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated January 25, 2024 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Register of Demands
  as follows:

  City of Cerritos  January 25, 2024  $6,816,544.76 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Continuance of the existence of a local emergency concerning a gasoline leak from a
  privately owned existing pipeline on the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine public golf course, and
  potential threat to the safety of persons and property requiring remediation, repair, and
  improvement of the public golf course and other City-owned public property, as specified
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Continue the local emergency as proclaimed in Resolution No. 2023-05, at the Cerritos
  Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course and the nearby City property with the C-4 well site;

  2. Make the findings set forth in Sections one (1) through eight (8) of Resolution No.
  2023-05, and incorporate by reference those findings, as they relate to the continued
  existence of a local emergency as specified; and

  3. Direct staff to provide a report to the City Council regarding the local emergency at
  least once every sixty (60) days, pursuant to Section 8630(c) of the California
  Government Code, until the City Council terminates the local emergency (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Award of contract for annual traffic engineering services in the City of Cerritos, RFP No.
  1525-23* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Sections 15061(b)(3) and 15378(b)(5) of the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA) Guidelines, the contract is exempt from CEQA Review.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, January 25, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Award a contract to Hartzog & Crabill, Inc. for annual traffic engineering services in the
  City of Cerritos, RFP No. 1525-23 for a twelve-month term, with provisions for four (4),
  twelve-month extensions, and reject the other proposals; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any project-related change orders,
  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Award of contract for annual civil engineering services in the City of Cerritos, RFP No. 1526-
  23* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Sections 15061(b)(3) and 15378(b)(5) of the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA) Guidelines, the contract is exempt from CEQA Review.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Award a contract to Willdan Engineering for annual civil engineering services in the City
  of Cerritos, RFP No. 1526-23, for a twelve-month term, with provisions for four (4),
  twelve-month extensions, and reject the other proposals; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any project-related change orders,
  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7F.  Waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS ACCEPTING AN EASEMENT DEED FOR PUBLIC UTILITY PURPOSES FROM CBG
  INVESTMENT PROPERTY AND RONALD W. GREGOIRE FAMILY TRUST, OWNERS OF THE
  PROPERTY LOCATED AT 11011 SOUTH STREET, CERRITOS, CA 90703 (APN 7038-013-
  018)* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines,
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, January 25, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7F.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2024-05, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ACCEPTING AN EASEMENT DEED
  FOR PUBLIC UTILITY PURPOSES FROM CBG INVESTMENT PROPERTY AND
  RONALD W. GREGOIRE FAMILY TRUST, OWNERS OF THE PROPERTY LOCATED
  AT 11011 SOUTH STREET, CERRITOS, CA 90703 (APN 7038-013-018)
  (COUNCIL); and

  2. Authorize the City Clerk to record the easement documents (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of a comprehensive assessment of the City’s existing
  transportation services, the Cerritos on Wheels (COW) fixed-route service and the Dial-A-
  Ride demand-response service, and a request for City Council direction regarding potential
  modifications to the City’s transportation services (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Sabrina Chan, Advance Planning Manager and the City’s
  transportation consultant Jim Moore, Program Manager, Moore and Associates, Inc. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Attorney to provide information to the City
  Council on the issues related to an unfunded State mandate, prohibited by the State
  Constitution, as they relate to conversion to alternative fuel vehicles by transportation
  providers.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Brian Tom spoke in support of maintaining the Dial-A-Ride demand-response service, or a
  similar curb-to-curb service, to provide safe and accessible public transit for disabled and
  senior residents of Cerritos.

  Catherine Pascual spoke in support of a demand-response micro-transit service in the City,
  and the provision of safe and accessible public transit for the disabled and senior
  community.

  Jim Tiao spoke in support of maintaining the Dial-A-Ride demand-response service, or a
  similar service, to provide safe and accessible public transit for the disabled and senior
  community.

  Written Correspondence:

  Don and Evelyn Mildner requested the continuance of COW fixed-route service and a
  restoration of pre-COVID service hours.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, January 25, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 8

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period and public
  hearing closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to direct staff to:

  1. Work with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) to
  determine an alternative or best use of a $4.4 million grant that was previously
  awarded to the City for the purchase of zero emission transit buses in support of fixed-
  route transit operations, including the purchase of "green" vehicles and/or use in
  support of a micro-transit service, and provide an update to the City Council
  accordingly;

  2. Establish parameters for amending the existing Cerritos on Wheels (COW) fixed-route
  service, in pursuit of a micro-transit demand-response COW service available to the
  general public, and maintain a separate demand-response Dial-A-Ride service for
  transportation of Cerritos seniors and persons with disabilities; and

  3. Solicit proposals for contract services for the implementation of a micro-transit
  demand-response COW service available to the general public City-wide with access to
  the Metro Green “C” Line and Metrolink stations in the city of Norwalk, as well as a
  separate micro-transit demand-response Dial-A-Ride service for Cerritos seniors and
  persons with disabilities (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of Budget Study Session No. 1 – Updating the Cerritos City
  Council on the status of the City's FY 2024-25 budget preparation process, and considering
  potential objectives for achieving the City Council's priority goals for the upcoming fiscal
  year and inclusion in the FY 2024-25 Combined Financial Program (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Budget Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Approve the proposed updates to the titles for Goals 1 and 2, the proposed goal
  descriptions, and the proposed objectives with their corresponding funding allocations
  for incorporation into the FY 2024-25 Budget, as follows:

(minutes continue on the next page)

  G1-01: Maintain accelerated rehabilitation of arterial streets that are in poor

  G1-02: Maintain accelerated rehabilitation of residential streets that are in poor

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Johnson, Vo, and Yokoyama, Mayor Pro Tem
